effectList: Release is not conditioned on paying money bail when operative law says so.
Judge evaluates lawful detention grounds from case/person records.
Release/detention affects custody, work availability and household presence.

laws.reverseOnRepeal: Repeal changes future proceedings according to operative law. Existing orders and final case outcomes do not automatically reverse.

existingLinkResearch.result: Table 4 fully controlled 2SLS: release -0.156 probability points, SE 0.034; detained mean 0.571.
existingLinkResearch.breadth: Marginal defendants affected by randomly assigned bail judges in Philadelphia and Miami-Dade; release versus detention.
existingLinkResearch.access: Working paper full text and Table 4 read.
existingLinkResearch.missingFigure: Need the final AER table interval, conviction baseline among the affected marginal defendants, and a defined detention input unit. Reversing a release effect and dividing by the whole detained mean does not establish the effect of detention on every defendant.

existingLinkResearch.result: Table 7 fully controlled 2SLS: release +0.037 employment probability points (SE 0.043) in years 1 to 2, +0.102 (SE 0.053) in years 3 to 4.
existingLinkResearch.breadth: Same marginal defendant population; tax-record formal employment, not all work.
existingLinkResearch.access: Working paper full text and Table 7 read.
existingLinkResearch.missingFigure: Need final published estimates and intervals, affected-defendant employment baseline, and distinct follow-up exposure records. The first-period imprecise estimate is not evidence of zero; a single immediate lag cannot represent both periods.
